topic: Word Swap (Verbal Ability and Reading Comprehension)

sections.title: Concept of Level 2 Word Swap
sections.content: In Level 2 Word Swap questions, the words may be grammatically correct but the meaning or tone of the sentence becomes incorrect. Often, the words belong to the same category (such as nouns or adjectives), so the mistake can only be detected through context. The goal is to identify which two words should be exchanged to make the sentence logical and natural.

sections.title: Context-Based Meaning Check
sections.content: Step 1: Understand the main idea of the entire sentence. Step 2: Identify the word that does not match the context. Step 3: Find another word in the sentence that fits better in that position. Step 4: Swap the two words and read the sentence again to check the meaning. Example: 'The policy created hope among critics and concern among supporters.' Swapping 'hope' and 'concern' may create a more logical meaning.

sections.title: Tone and Editorial Language
sections.content: Step 1: Identify whether the sentence has a positive or negative tone. Step 2: Recognize the emotional tone of the words (positive or negative). Step 3: Detect the word that carries the wrong tone. Step 4: After swapping, check whether the tone and context align properly. Example: 'The success of the mission caused disappointment among the team.' In such cases, words like success or failure may change the context.

sections.title: Logical Relationship Between Words
sections.content: Step 1: Identify the relationship between words such as cause-effect, contrast, or result. Step 2: Determine which word seems misplaced. Step 3: Swap it with the word that logically fits in that position. Step 4: Read the new sentence to verify whether the logical flow improves.

sections.title: Editorial Sentence Analysis
sections.content: Step 1: Break the sentence into smaller parts. Step 2: Understand the meaning of each part. Step 3: Identify the word that does not match the idea of that part. Step 4: After swapping, check whether the meaning continues smoothly.

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content: 1. Making decisions based only on grammar. 2. Ignoring the overall context of the sentence. 3. Overlooking the tone or emotional meaning of words. 4. Not re-reading the sentence after swapping.

sections.title: Quick Summary
sections.content: In Level 2 Word Swap questions, context and tone are more important than grammar. To find the correct answer, it is essential to understand the main idea of the sentence, recognize the tone of words, and check the logical relationship between them.

tricks.title: Context First Trick
tricks.explanation: First understand the main idea of the entire sentence and then analyze the position of the words.
tricks.example: If the sentence is about criticism, positive words may appear out of place.

tricks.title: Tone Matching Trick
tricks.explanation: Positive words should appear in positive contexts and negative words in negative contexts.
tricks.example: Success usually goes with celebration, while failure goes with concern.

tricks.title: Swap and Re-read Method
tricks.explanation: Swap the suspected pair of words and read the sentence again.
tricks.example: If the sentence sounds more natural after swapping, it is likely correct.

tricks.title: Editorial Logic Trick
tricks.explanation: Editorial sentences often show cause and effect relationships.

tricks.title: Opposite Tone Detection
tricks.explanation: If two words have opposite tones, they may be incorrectly placed.
tricks.example: Identifying misplaced words like hope and fear.

tricks.title: Meaning Group Trick
tricks.explanation: Identify words that belong to the same meaning group.
tricks.example: Progress and development belong to the same conceptual group.

tricks.title: Sentence Flow Check
tricks.explanation: After swapping, check whether the sentence flows naturally.
tricks.example: Editorial sentences should show smooth logical progression.

tricks.title: Elimination Strategy
tricks.explanation: Remove the words that already seem correct and focus on the remaining ones.
tricks.example: First identify the words that clearly fit their positions.
